overview: This paper proposes Targeted Reasoning Unlearning (TRU), a method that achieves controllable and explainable LLM unlearning by combining cross-entropy supervised loss on reasoning-based unlearning targets with Gradient Difference loss to specify the unlearning scope and post-unlearning responses.

modules.name: Reasoning Target Generation Pipeline
modules.description: Module to construct task-specific prompts for WMDP/MUSE/TOFU benchmarks and interact with advanced reasoning models (e.g., Deepseek-reasoner) to generate reasoning-based unlearning targets, producing triplets of original data, reasoning traces, and refusal responses.

modules.name: Dataset Construction and Dataloader
modules.description: Module to define custom PyTorch Datasets for both unlearning and retention data. It handles the tokenization, padding, and structural formatting of triplets, ensuring proper alignment for the LLM input and the separation of reasoning traces and refusal responses using special tokens.

modules.name: LLM Backbone and Tokenizer Adaptation
modules.description: Module to load the base LLM backbones (e.g., Llama, Zephyr) and expand their tokenizer vocabulary with specific structural tokens (e.g., think and answer tags) to enable reasoning before generating an answer, along with resizing the model's embedding layer.

modules.name: Unlearning Target Loss Implementation
modules.description: Module to implement the cross-entropy supervised loss function that maximizes the likelihood of the reasoning trace and the refusal response conditioned on the in-scope query, enforcing the specified scope and response behavior.

modules.name: GA-based Loss Implementation
modules.description: Module to implement the Gradient Difference (GradDiff) baseline loss, which penalizes the likelihood of the unlearning dataset while encouraging the likelihood of the retention dataset to ensure thorough knowledge erasure.

modules.name: TRU Joint Optimization Engine
modules.description: Module to combine the Unlearning Target Loss and the GA-based Loss using a balancing hyperparameter. It manages the forward propagation, joint loss computation, backward propagation, and gradient updates during the unlearning training loop.

modules.name: Standard Benchmark Evaluation
modules.description: Module to evaluate unlearned models using traditional metrics, calculating QA accuracy on WMDP subsets, performance on MMLU for retention, and specific accuracy/entropy metrics for MUSE and TOFU benchmarks.

modules.name: LLM-as-a-Judge (LaaJ) Evaluation Pipeline
modules.description: Module to implement the unified LaaJ evaluation framework. It constructs evaluation prompts for an external powerful LLM to score model responses across Unlearning Quality (Relevance, Rejection, Helpfulness) and Retention Quality (Readability, Specificity, Logic), parsing the structured JSON output.

modules.name: Attack Simulation Module
modules.description: Module to evaluate robustness by implementing attack scenarios: cross-lingual attacks (translating queries using GPT), jailbreak attacks (prepending specific adversarial prompts), and relearning attacks (few-shot fine-tuning on unlearning samples).

modules.name: Baseline Methods Implementation
modules.description: Module to implement comparison baselines including Gradient Ascent, GradDiff, KL divergence, Preference Optimization, Weighted Gradient Ascent, Negative Preference Optimization, and Representation Misdirection for Unlearning.

modules.name: Ablation Study and Hyperparameter Analysis Runner
modules.description: Module to conduct controlled variable experiments by removing or replacing key components (e.g., reasoning traces, target loss, criteria) and performing sensitivity analysis on the balancing hyperparameter to validate the contribution of each module.
